metadata.title: Lamentations
metadata.subtitle: Lamentations 1:1 – 5:22 (18 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Lamentations according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: How does the Book of Lamentations begin (Lamentations 1:1)?

options.text: With lamentation over the burning of the temple and the spoiling of holy vessels
How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! she is become as a widow
With mourning over the captivity of the king's sons and the end of the royal line
With crying over the grievous famine in the land and the bitter death of the cattle

questions.text: What comfort is declared in the midst of affliction in Lamentations 3:22-23?

options.text: The walls of Zion shall be built again, and the fierce heathen shall retreat afar
It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed; they are new every morning
The judgment of the holy God shall never fall again, for he hath forgiven all iniquity
The former royal glory shall return without repentance, for the LORD will not forget

questions.text: What prayer does the people make at the end of the book (Lamentations 5:21)?

options.text: Turn thou us unto thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old
Restore the sacred treasures of the temple and let the priests minister at altar
Smite all our adversaries with the sword and destroy them that have afflicted us
Establish the kingdom of our fathers again and set a son of David upon the throne

questions.text: What cry does the city direct unto all that pass by (Lamentations 1:12)?

options.text: Help us to build the broken gates again; for our affliction is grievous
Pass by in haste and look not upon us; for the sorrow of Zion is great
Behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow done unto me
Make a peace with the princes of Babylon; for our wound cannot be healed

questions.text: How does Lamentations 2:1 describe the anger of the Lord upon Zion?

options.text: The Lord hath given Zion space to repent and hath deferred his anger
The Lord hath spared Zion and turned away his anger from her
The Lord hath cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel
The Lord hath smitten Zion with hail and with locusts

questions.text: What does the writer lament concerning the young children in Lamentations 2:11?

options.text: That they were led away into cruel captivity in a foreign land
That they grew up without any faithful teacher or understanding
That the young children and sucklings swoon in the city streets
That they remained fatherless without any helper to succour them

questions.text: What is the daughter of Zion commanded to do in Lamentations 2:19?

options.text: Arise in the night, and pour out thine heart like water before the Lord
Rest quietly until the morning dawn, until the Lord heareth thy petition
Guard the walls by night and defend the royal gates against every enemy
Treat with the adversaries and bring rich presents that they may depart

questions.text: What is declared to be good according to Lamentations 3:26-27?

options.text: To bring tithes faithfully and offer all sacrifices according to the law
To dwell within the sanctuary and never depart from the holy courts of God
To search the scriptures continually and teach the commandments to children
To quietly wait for salvation of the LORD, and bear the yoke in his youth

questions.text: With what imagery does Lamentations 4 begin its lamentation?

options.text: The gold is become dim, and the stones of the sanctuary are poured out
The swords are broken, and the shields of the mighty are cast in Kidron
The fruitful vines are trodden down, and the grapes of the land are sour
The tents of the enemy stand round about, and the watchmen have all fled

questions.text: What distress of the women is recorded in Lamentations 4:10?

options.text: Pitiful women sold all their jewels for bread to nourish their little ones
Pitiful women left their children at the temple that they might find bread
Pitiful women fled with their children over the mountains to heathen lands
The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children to eat them

questions.text: How is the captive king designated in Lamentations 4:20?

options.text: The shield and buckler of the people
The breath, the anointed of the LORD
The mighty lion of the tribe of Judah
The faithful shepherd of the heritage

questions.text: What confession does the congregation make in Lamentations 5:19?

options.text: Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and therefore no hope is left for us
The heathen nations shall rebuild our walls and restore the gates of Zion
We will offer burnt offerings as soon as the king of Babylon granteth peace
Thou, O LORD, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation

questions.text: What happened to the friends of the weeping city (Lamentations 1:2)?

options.text: They dealt treacherously with her and are become her enemies
They remained faithful to her and brought bread into her home
They held their peace and waited to see who would win battle
They fled into foreign lands and returned not until the fall

questions.text: What does the soul of the afflicted declare in Lamentations 3:24?

options.text: The LORD is my rock; therefore will I not be moved
The LORD is my portion; therefore will I hope in him
The LORD is my light; therefore will I not be faint
The LORD is my shepherd; therefore will I not fear

questions.text: How does the Lord deal with the children of men (Lamentations 3:31-32)?

options.text: He afflicteth willingly and casteth off the sons of men for ever
He causeth sorrow without a cause and hath no mercy upon the sad
Though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion in his mercy
He spareth all the children of men and executeth no judgment now

questions.text: To what self-examination does Lamentations 3:40 call?

options.text: Search out the transgressions of our fathers and bear all their guilt
Search the book of the law and submit ourselves unto the earthly king
Examine the devices of our adversaries and prepare for a great battle
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again unto the LORD our God

questions.text: With what does Lamentations 4:6 compare the punishment of the daughter of my people?

options.text: It is greater than the punishment of the sin of Sodom
It is greater than the punishment of the sin of Babel
It is equal unto the punishment of the sin of Gomorrah
It is greater than the punishment of the sin of Nineveh

questions.text: With what does Lamentations 4:19 compare the persecutors of the people?

options.text: More numerous than the locusts in the field
Swifter than the eagles of the holy heaven
More fierce than the young lions in forest
Swifter than the swift horses of the battle
